article.headline: Scores from last Night: North Pike wins by one; Ocean Springs and Greene County stay perfect
article.html:
North Pike escaped Florence with a one-point boys basketball victory, while Ocean Springs and Greene County protected unbeaten starts in very different ways Saturday. The Jaguars won 48–47, the Greyhounds beat Pace 71–51, and Greene County’s girls survived Heidelberg 30–29.

Other November 21, 2026, finals included Greenwood handing Horn Lake’s girls their first reported loss, Olive Branch’s girls staying unbeaten and Kosciusko completing a basketball sweep. On the soccer field, New Albany held off Clinton and Corinth’s boys finished with a pair of draws. Records below are the figures currently listed on the completed matchup reports.

North Pike and Florence split after a one-point boys finish

North Pike edged Florence 48–47 in the boys tournament game, leaving the Jaguars listed at 5–1 and the Eagles at 1–3. The narrow final gave North Pike the win in the closer of the varsity basketball meetings between the schools.

Florence took the girls game, beating North Pike 54–42. The completed report lists the Eagles at 5–1 and the Jaguars at 4–2. Both fixtures had been highlighted in our Saturday Games To Watch preview.

Ocean Springs rolls; Greene County wins narrowly

Ocean Springs beat Pace, Florida, 71–51 in a neutral-site boys basketball game and is listed at 7–0. Pace is 1–1. The Greyhounds preserved their perfect opening against an out-of-state opponent, with a substantially wider final margin than the one that kept Greene County unbeaten.

Greene County’s girls held off Heidelberg 30–29 in a tournament game. The Wildcats are listed at 7–0, while Heidelberg is 2–4. The one-point result kept Greene County’s record unblemished.

Greenwood ends Horn Lake’s perfect start; Olive Branch stays unbeaten

Greenwood defeated Horn Lake 51–36 in girls basketball and is listed at 6–0. Horn Lake is 6–1 after its first reported defeat. Greenwood won every quarter, taking the opening period 13–8 and the second 11–10 before extending its advantage after halftime.

Olive Branch’s girls won 65–42 at Columbus to reach a listed 3–0 record. Columbus is 1–4. The Conquistadors carried an unbeaten start into the road game and left with it intact, producing another clear final margin in the selected girls basketball results.

Kosciusko sweeps; Columbus boys answer

Kosciusko beat Holmes County Central 68–22 in boys basketball and won the girls game 54–36. The Whippets’ boys remain unbeaten at a listed 4–0, and their girls are 4–1. Holmes County Central’s corresponding records are 0–7 and 1–6 after the sweep.

Columbus’ boys defeated Northwest Rankin 74–56 in a separate nonconference game. The Falcons are listed at 5–1 and the Cougars at 3–3, giving Columbus a boys victory on a day when its girls lost to Olive Branch.

DeSoto results: Horn Lake boys win; Jaguars split

Horn Lake’s boys won 63–48 at Greenwood, giving the schools a basketball split. The Eagles lost the first quarter 15–12 but took the second 19–10 and closed with a 12–4 fourth period. Horn Lake is listed at 4–3 and Greenwood at 5–2.

DeSoto Central’s girls beat West Memphis, Arkansas, 35–28 at a neutral site. The Jaguars won the first three quarters, including a 9–4 opening period, and are listed at 1–2. West Memphis outscored DeSoto Central 8–5 in the fourth but finished short.

Gulfport won the boys game at DeSoto Central 63–51 and stayed unbeaten at a listed 4–0. DeSoto Central’s boys are 2–2. For additional area results from the preceding night, see our Friday scores and playoff recap.

New Albany holds off Clinton in boys soccer

New Albany beat Clinton 3–2 and is listed at 7–2. The Bulldogs led 1–0 at halftime, and each team scored twice in the second half. That opening-half advantage supplied the difference in the final; Clinton is listed at 2–3–1.

Corinth boys draw twice at Richland showcase

Corinth’s boys drew 1–1 with both Pass Christian and Richland at Ranger Stadium during the North vs. South soccer showcase. Against the Pirates, the Warriors led 1–0 at halftime before Pass Christian equalized in the second half. Alcorn County Sports reports that the two draws left Corinth at 2–5–2.

Corinth’s girls were held scoreless in both of their verified matches, losing 5–0 to Pass Christian and 4–0 to Richland. The boys avoided defeat in both fixtures, but neither Corinth varsity team recorded a win in the reported showcase results.

Amory takes both Richland games

Amory’s boys beat Richland 3–1 and drew 0–0 with Pass Christian. The completed matchup pages list the Panthers at 6–2–1 after the day’s results. They scored in the win over Richland and then kept a clean sheet in the scoreless meeting with the Pirates.

Amory’s girls beat Richland 1–0 with the only goal coming in the second half. Pass Christian won their other reported match 2–0. Amory therefore finished its Richland meetings with wins in both divisions, while the Pass Christian fixtures produced a boys draw and a girls defeat.

Lewisburg and Tupelo split Florida soccer results

Lewisburg’s girls beat Choctawhatchee 4–0 in Fort Walton Beach, scoring twice in each half. The Patriots’ boys lost 3–0 to the same school. Lewisburg’s listed records are 5–4 for the girls and 4–4 for the boys after the split.

Tupelo’s girls won 5–0 at Gulf Breeze and are listed at 6–1. The Golden Wave boys lost 4–0 at Fort Walton Beach, which scored twice in each half. Tupelo’s boys are listed at 4–1 after their first reported defeat.

Ocean Springs wins in both soccer divisions

Ocean Springs paired its boys basketball victory with soccer wins in both divisions. The boys beat Northwest Rankin 3–1 and are listed at 5–2–1. The girls won 4–0 at St. Andrew’s Episcopal and are listed at 2–2–3. Both soccer fixtures were reported as nonconference matches.
